lines: One attack at THAC0 15 for 2d6 damage.

gm.title: Special rules
lines: Flight. It can carry up to 200 lb. in flight. Unencumbered, save vs. paralyzation after each hour of flight. A failed save forces half an hour of rest per two previous hours of flight. A rider lowers maneuverability from C to D and calls for a save every half hour. After losing 50% or more of its HP, it cannot fly. It can glide until it has lost 75% or more. Wings are covered with fine fur and have the same vulnerability to fire as the rest of the body. Under the appendix’s maneuverability rules, C and D must maintain at least half their speed to stay aloft. C can turn up to 90 degrees per round and attack once every two rounds. D can turn up to 60 degrees and make one pass every three rounds. The lupasus often attacks from the ground.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One bite per round, 3d4 damage. On an unmodified roll of 20, the bite severs a hand or foot from an attacking human-sized or smaller creature. The entry gives no separate save against severing. It rarely bites without severe provocation unless trained to attack on command.

gm.title: Armor and movement
lines: Head and back are AC 5. Opponents near the extremities are treated as targeting the legs at AC 6. It has no shell to retract into. A male out of water takes a −2 penalty on attack rolls and 2 damage per round from dryness. They can run for days without rest and keep swimming indefinitely at half movement. Maximum load is 600 lb. at full speed, 900 lb. at half speed or 1,200 lb. at one-third speed.

lines: Nikt’oos gain Legacies and need cinnabryl to avert Affliction. Most have little access to it, so Affliction is common. The entry gives no fixed Legacy.

gm.title: Encounters and ecology
lines: Uncommon, solitary, one appearing. Active by day. Tortles and snappers often domesticate them as amphibious mounts or beasts of burden. Wild ones usually flee humanoids but become aggressive in mating season. A female buries 5d6 eggs yearly above the high tide line on a warm beach. Males normally stay in water and may come ashore to defend an egg-laying female. They eat jellyfish, mollusks and seaweed. Adults live about 90 years in the wild or up to 150 in captivity. Fewer than 5% of wild offspring reach adulthood.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Hold Breath. Outside water, the octopus can hold its breath for 1 hour.
Underwater Camouflage. Underwater, its Stealth score is 18.
Water Breathing. The octopus breathes only underwater.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Tentacles. Make a melee weapon attack at +5 against one target within 15 ft. A hit deals 10 (2d6 + 3) bludgeoning damage. A Huge or smaller creature hit is Grappled (escape DC 13) and Restrained until the grapple ends. The octopus can grapple up to two creatures at once.

gm.title: Bonus Actions
lines: Tentacle Slam. Slam one Medium or smaller creature the octopus is grappling against a solid surface. The creature makes a DC 13 Strength save, taking 7 (2d6) bludgeoning damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Reactions
lines: Ink Dash (Recharge 4–6). When a creature the octopus can see damages it, the octopus can release a 20-ft.-radius cloud of ink centered on itself if it is underwater. The cloud heavily obscures the area until the end of the octopus’s next turn. A strong current can disperse it. The octopus can then swim up to its swim speed. If it swims, it immediately releases every creature it is grappling.

lines: A large toad with a broad mouth, warty back, and heavy hind legs.

gm.title: Other statistics

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Amphibious. Old Croaker breathes air and water.
Standing Leap. With or without a run, it can long jump 20 ft. or high jump 10 ft.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +4 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. A hit deals 7 (1d10 + 2) piercing plus 5 (1d10) poison damage and grapples the target, escape DC 13. Until the grapple ends, that target is restrained and Old Croaker can bite only that target.
Swallow. Make a Bite attack on a grappled target of Medium size or smaller. A hit ends the grapple and swallows the target. The swallowed creature is blinded and restrained, has total cover from outside attacks and effects, and takes 10 (3d6) acid damage at the start of each of Old Croaker’s turns. Old Croaker holds one swallowed target at once. When Old Croaker dies, the creature is no longer restrained and can move 5 ft. to emerge prone.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Old Croaker lurks under the freezing pool in Croaker Cave. Hulil trained it to ferry visitors across the pool one at a time.

gm.title: Encounter application
lines: A successful DC 15 Wisdom (Animal Handling) check can persuade Old Croaker to leave the party alone and carry the characters across individually.

gm.title: Source notes

gm.title: Tusks and forelegs
lines: Four attacks, each for 3–12 damage, using tusks and forelegs. The trunk cannot be used to fight. The oliphant can engage up to four man-sized foes, two ogre-sized foes, or one giant-sized foe simultaneously.

gm.title: Chessboard Rook
lines: Use the p. 11 preset for the Rook. Leather armor gives AC 2. Speed 15″, 10+5 HD, 65 HP and four attacks of 3–12 each. The Rook also has 25% magic resistance.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Avoids inhabited areas when solitary. A young specimen can be captured and trained, with mature trained males especially effective. War animals can wear reinforced armor and spikes and carry archers or pikemen in howdahs. Regular fire does not scare the animal unless the fire directly threatens it. When threatened an oliphant generally fights instead of fleeing.

gm.title: Groups and value
lines: When three or more appear, check each animal beyond the first two. The module gives a 25% chance of a calf and 75% for a half-grown animal. Young are split evenly between the sexes. A solitary animal is male, and any group has at most one mature male. Tusks are worth 100–400 gp each. Ivory is worth about 4 gp per pound.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: The generic oliphant and Chessboard Rook share the profile. The armor, fixed HP and 25% magic resistance are encounter-specific.
Generic oliphant level and XP are blank on p. 30. No numeric morale is printed.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A gray-brown pachyderm with four curved tusks, a short trunk and broad round ears.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Gore · melee · +9 to hit · reach 10 ft. · 4d6 + 6 slashing
Stomp · melee · +9 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 3d10 + 6 bludgeoning

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Siege Monster · It deals double damage to objects and structures.
Terrifying Siege · Destroying a Small or larger object forces every hostile creature within 10 ft. to make a DC 16 CHA save. A failed save frightens the creature until the end of its next turn.

Trampling Charge · After moving at least 20 ft. straight toward a creature and hitting it with Gore that turn, the target must pass a DC 16 STR save or fall prone. The warbeast can Stomp the target once as a bonus action if it is prone.
Condition resistance · The block lists resistance to frightened, prone.

gm.title: Action mechanics
lines: Multiattack · Make one Gore and one Stomp attack or make two Gore attacks.
Stomp · It can target only a prone creature.

gm.title: Bonus action mechanics
lines: Trunk Sweep · Creatures in a 15-ft. cone make a DC 16 STR save or fall prone.

gm.title: Companion use mechanics
lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 2,400 gp. It can carry 1,560 lb.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Black Flag fixed values are Perception 13 and Stealth 9. Ability modifiers are STR +9, DEX −1, CON +5, INT −4, WIS +0 and CHA −2. No languages or special senses.
The book spells it Oliphaunt Warbeast. The profile uses the existing catalog name and keeps the printed attack bonuses and damage.
The handling rule specifies an Animal Handling check, then calls its failure a failed save. Resolve failure using the check it specifies.
Source: Kobold Press, Player’s Guide 2 (2026), pp. 142–144.

gm.title: Hit point rule

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A large gray or black manatee relative with a flattened horizontal tail, short foreflippers ending in small webbed hands, and no external hind legs. Its small head has a straight snout and a bristly split upper lip. Males have two small tusklike incisors. Adults reach 9 to 11 ft. and up to 1,300 lb.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC 6 (10 unarmored). Morale steady (11–12). Low to very intelligent (5–12). Treasure K (F). No special defenses or magic resistance. The entry gives no individual saving throw values.

gm.title: Printed source

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One weapon attack per round for 1d8 damage. Omm-was favor nets underwater and use spears and tridents for defense. Some traded with Herathians for underwater crossbows.

gm.title: Burn Legacy
lines: Most omm-was have Burn. It activates as an instantaneous Legacy up to three times per day. A successful attack roll deals 1d4 plus 1 per level or HD. At the typical 3 HD that is 1d4 + 3 with a 2-ft. range. The range starts at touch and increases 1 ft. per level beyond first to 10 ft. maximum. The flame comes from a fixed hand or mouth and may ignite a flammable object even when the attack misses the target. Omm-was need cinnabryl to ward off Affliction. An omm-wa Afflicted with Burn overheats after a few seconds out of the water.

gm.title: Movement and senses
lines: Air-breathing and at home in salt or fresh water. It can leave the water for at most 30 minutes at a time. It sees more than 300 ft. in clear water and roughly as far as a human in air, though bright light bothers its eyes. It rarely dives below 100 ft.

gm.title: Encounter groups
lines: Rare, any activity cycle. Roll 1d4 + 2 or 1d6 + 14 appearing. A family includes one female shaman of levels 1–3. For every 30 omm-was add a fighter of levels 3–5. For every 60 add a warleader of effective fighter levels 5–8. For every 100 add a wise woman of priest levels 4–6. Shamans normally advance as priests to level 8. About one male in five can gain fighter levels. The rare twin pair is one female shaman, maximum level 8, and one male fighter protector, maximum level 10. Males have a 5% chance of a character kit, typically Defender.

gm.title: Society and ecology
lines: Females hold all authority and inherit their rank through the maternal line. Females reach maturity at 12. The family herbivores tend underwater farms and feed mainly at night. They gather mineral nodules, including a little cinnabryl, and record messages with pebble arrangements or knotted strings and beads.

lines: At the end of each character’s turn, roll on the printed Cat Chase Complications table. A hit against AC 12 makes contact without lasting damage. Spell-imposed conditions end automatically at the end of her next turn. To end the chase, all living characters must hide. A passive Perception of 15 spots the mouse hole within view of the fireplace. A character looking for a ground-level hiding place can attempt a DC 15 Wisdom (Perception) check with advantage from anywhere in the room.

lines: Cost and carrying capacity · 50 gp. It can carry 210 lb.

Handler commands · A designated handler can use an action and pass a DC 10 WIS (Animal Handling) check to order it to Attack, Dash, Disengage, Dodge, Help, Hide or Use an Object. On failure the animal defends itself and otherwise takes no action.
Delivering or fetching an item · Use an Object can deliver an item. It can also fetch an item from a willing creature or one on the ground or otherwise unworn and uncarried.

Training a handler · It can learn up to four handlers, with one week of training per handler. Teaching a fifth normally replaces the handler who last commanded it least recently. At the GM’s discretion, a close bond can prevent replacement and the new training fails.
Mounted combat · While used as a mount in mounted combat, it follows the controlled mount rules.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Two claws +13 melee (1d8 + 8 each) and bite +8 melee (2d6 + 4).

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Improved Grab (Ex). On a claw hit against a Medium or smaller opponent, deal normal damage and attempt a grapple as a free action. No touch attack or attack of opportunity. A successful hold pulls the target into the bear’s space without provoking. Grapple normally at +18, or hold with the claw alone at a -20 penalty to grapple checks. A claw-only hold leaves the bear free to use other attacks, threaten squares and keep its Dexterity bonus to AC. The initial hold adds no damage. In later rounds, each successful grapple check deals the claw damage again. The bear may drag the opponent if its carrying capacity allows. The target can replace an attack with an opposed grapple check to escape, or use a standard action to oppose the bear’s grapple check with Escape Artist.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines: Low-light vision retains color and detail at twice normal human range in dim light. Scent detects creatures within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors, triple for overpowering ones. Use a move action to learn the direction and approach within 5 ft. to pinpoint. With Track, use Wisdom or Survival to follow scent. A fresh trail typically starts at DC 10, increasing by 2 per hour since it was made. Scent tracking ignores surface and visibility modifiers.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Hide -2, Listen +5, Spot +7, Swim +16. Endurance, Run, Track. Add +12 to Hide in snow, for +10 total there. Swim includes the +8 racial bonus for special actions or avoiding hazards. It can take 10 on Swim while distracted or endangered and can run while swimming straight.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Cold plains. Solitary or pair. The polar bear is long and lean and slightly taller than a brown bear. It relies mainly on its claws when fighting. Always neutral. No treasure.

Flyby Attack · At-will standard action. Fly up to 8 squares and make one melee basic attack along that route. Moving away from that target does not provoke its opportunity attacks.

lines: August 2012 update, p. 77, changes the original size from Tiny to Small. The checked Deluxe page already shows Small.
Unaligned. No languages. It communicates with animal noises. Wild pseudodragons hunt other creatures and usually leave humanoids alone unless provoked. Some live with humanoids as pets.
The tactics use Sting during a Flyby Attack when it is available. Against a persistent enemy the pseudodragon shifts, then uses Invisibility.

lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersS.rtf, RAT SWARM. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/swarm.htm#ratSwarm

gm.title: Attack
lines: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. At the end of its movement, deal damage automatically to each creature whose space it shares. There is no attack roll or miss chance for concealment or cover. The attack is nonmagical.

gm.title: Full attack
lines: Swarm, 1d6 plus disease. The automatic Swarm Attack uses the same rules in both entries.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Disease (Ex). Filth fever is delivered by the swarm attack. Make an immediate DC 12 Fortitude save to prevent infection. On a failure, after 1d3 days take 1d3 Dex and 1d3 Con damage. Save at DC 12 daily afterward or repeat the ability damage. Two successes in a row clear the disease.
Distraction (Ex). A living creature that begins its turn in the swarm’s square makes a DC 12 Fortitude save or is nauseated for 1 round. A nauseated creature can take only one move action per turn and cannot attack, cast spells or concentrate. The shared subtype wording specifies living creatures vulnerable to the swarm’s damage. Both printed triggers are recorded here.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim light, with color and detail.
Scent. Detect by smell out to 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind or 15 ft. downwind. Double those ranges for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action gives the direction. Pinpoint the source within 5 ft.
Tiny swarm. Halve damage from slashing and piercing weapons. It cannot be critically hit or flanked. The swarm cannot grapple or be grappled, tripped, or bull rushed. It breaks up at 0 HP or below and does not become staggered or dying from damage. Losing HP above 0 does not reduce its attack or defenses.

gm.title: Swarm movement
lines: One nonflying Tiny swarm represents about 300 rats and uses one set of stats and saves. It can cover any four contiguous squares and fit through gaps a constituent rat can use. It shares spaces with creatures of any size and can pass through them. Moving into or through an opponent’s space can provoke an attack of opportunity. The swarm does not threaten creatures or make attacks of opportunity.

gm.title: Swarm spell and effect rules
lines: Immune to effects that target a fixed number of creatures. The shared mind-affecting exception requires intelligence and a hive mind, and this block lists no hive mind. Area effects deal 50% extra damage. Casting a spell or maintaining concentration in the swarm’s area requires a Concentration check at DC 20 + spell level. Skills requiring patience or focus require a DC 20 Concentration check. An improvised lit torch deals 1d3 fire on a hit, and a broken thrown lit lantern deals 1d4 fire in adjacent squares. A weapon’s added energy damage applies in full. Sufficient damage reduction and incorporeality can prevent the swarm attack’s ordinary damage.

gm.title: Nonlethal dispersal
lines: If nonlethal damage renders the swarm unconscious it disperses until its HP exceed its nonlethal damage.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines: Balance +10, Climb +10, Hide +14, Listen +6, Spot +7, Swim +10. Racial bonuses are +4 on Hide and Move Silently, +8 on Balance, Climb and Swim. The swarm uses Dex for Climb and Swim. It can take 10 on Climb and Swim even under pressure and can run while swimming straight. Feats are Alertness and Weapon Finesse.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Any environment. Solitary, pack of 2–4 swarms, or infestation of 7–12 swarms. It surrounds warm-blooded prey. No advancement, level adjustment, or treasure.

gm.title: Printed discrepancies
lines: The RTF gives 13 HP for 4d8, whose usual mean is 18. Use the listed HP 13. The creature and subtype use different phrasing for the Distraction trigger, as shown above.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A sturdy white-and-brown working dog with a dark facial mask, drooping ears, thick paws, and a fitted riding saddle.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC 16 (+2 Dexterity, +4 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 14. Base attack +1, grapple +3. Space 5 ft., reach 5 ft. Fort +5, Ref +5, Will +1.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, DOG, RIDING. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/dogRiding.htm

gm.title: Attack
lines: Bite +3 melee, 1d6 + 3 piercing, slashing, and bludgeoning.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: War-trained Trip (Ex). A war-trained riding dog can attempt a trip as a free action after a bite hit, without a touch attack or attack of opportunity. Target a Large or smaller foe. Use the dog’s Strength check at +2 against the defender’s better Strength or Dexterity check, with the usual size and stability modifiers. A win makes the target prone. Failure grants the foe no counter-trip. Mounted combat. The dog can attack while carrying a rider. A rider on a war-trained mount can make a DC 10 Ride check as a free action to also attack.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. In dim illumination, sees twice as far as a human and keeps color and detail.
Scent. Detect ordinary creatures within 30 ft., 60 ft. upwind, or 15 ft. downwind. Double those distances for strong odors and triple them for overpowering odors. A move action identifies the direction, and within 5 ft. the animal pinpoints the source.
Track by scent. Take the Track feat’s usual checks, with DC 10 for a typical fresh trail and +2 DC per hour since it was left. Surface conditions and poor visibility do not affect scent tracking. Odor strength and number of creatures can shift the DC.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Jump +8, Listen +5, Spot +5, Swim +3, Survival +1. Feats. Alertness, Track (bonus feat).
The entry prints a +4 racial Jump bonus and Jump +8 in the table. Survival has a +4 racial bonus when tracking by scent, for +5 total.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines:
Temperate plains. Solitary or pack of 5–12. Always neutral, no treasure. No advancement listed. No level adjustment.
Covers breeds such as collies, huskies and St. Bernards. Light load up to 100 lb., medium 101–200 lb., heavy 201–300 lb., and maximum drag 1,500 lb.

gm.title: Source notes
lines:
The skills table prints Jump +8. At 40 ft. speed, the shared Jump rule would add +4 to the dog’s +2 Strength and +4 racial bonus even before ranks. The summary retains the printed +8.
The dog entry references Wolf for the procedure. The +2 trip check uses the dog’s own Strength and Medium size. The wolf’s printed +1 is wolf-specific.

gm.title: Feat mechanics
lines: Flyby Attack · While flying, take a standard action at any point during one move. The roc cannot take a second move action that round.

Snatch · On a talon or bite hit, the roc can start a grapple as with Improved Grab. Against a target three or more sizes smaller, it deals automatic damage from the grabbing weapon each round. It can drop the target as a free action or fling it 1d6 × 10 ft. as a standard action. Fling damage is 1d6 per 10 ft. traveled, or falling damage if greater while airborne.
Wingover · Once per round while flying, spend 10 ft. of movement to turn up to 180 degrees as a free action. It may dive during a wingover but cannot gain altitude that round.

Power Attack · Before attack rolls, trade up to 13 points of melee attack bonus for an equal bonus to melee damage until the roc’s next turn. The secondary Bite’s listed penalty already reflects Multiattack.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Forest Rot. When the Rotbeast dies, each non-Fungus creature within 5 ft. makes a DC 13 Constitution save. On a failure, it gains one level of Exhaustion and contracts forest rot.
Forest rot halves the HP a creature recovers by spending Hit Dice or finishing a long rest. It prevents the normal long-rest reduction in Exhaustion. On finishing each long rest, the infected creature makes a DC 13 Constitution save. Failure adds one level of Exhaustion. Success removes one level, and the creature recovers from forest rot if that success leaves its Exhaustion below 1.
Rotwake. Each space the Rotbeast leaves is difficult terrain for 24 hours for creatures other than rotbeasts. A non-Fungus creature that enters such a space for the first time on a turn or starts its turn there makes a DC 13 Constitution save. It takes 3 (1d6) poison damage on a failure or half as much on a success.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Bite · melee · +4 to hit · reach 5 ft. · 1d2−2 piercing, slashing and bludgeoning

gm.title: Special attack mechanics
lines: Poison (Ex) · After a damaging bite, the target makes a Fortitude save immediately and again 1 minute later, even if the first save succeeds. Each failure deals 1d6 Constitution damage. The viper is immune to its own venom and to venom from others of its kind. · DC 10 Fortitude

gm.title: Trait mechanics
lines: Scent (Ex) · Detect creatures by smell within 30 ft., 60 ft. if the creature is upwind or 15 ft. if downwind. A move action reveals the direction. Within 5 ft., the viper can pinpoint the creature.

Snake skills · The listed modifiers include racial bonuses of +4 to Hide, Listen and Spot and +8 to Balance and Climb. Use the higher of Strength and Dexterity for Climb. The viper can take 10 on Climb checks even when rushed or threatened.
Swim · The listed Swim modifier includes a +8 racial bonus for hazards and special maneuvers. The viper can take 10 even when distracted or in danger, and can run in a straight line while swimming.

gm.title: Table notes
lines: Always neutral. Solitary. The SRD lists no advancement or level adjustment. The viper usually bites defensively and then retreats.
Weapon Finesse uses Dexterity on the Bite attack roll. The listed attack bonus already uses Dexterity.

Use initiative +3 and the listed Weapon Finesse feat for this SRD printing. The later Monster Manual errata makes Weapon Finesse a bonus feat and adds Improved Initiative. d20srd.org reflects those changes and gives initiative +7.
Roll the printed Bite damage. If the result is below 1, the hit deals 1 damage before applying defenses.

Spider Climb. It can climb difficult surfaces, including ceilings upside down, without an ability check.
Web Sense. While touching a web, it knows the exact location of any other creature touching the same web.
Web Walker. It ignores movement restrictions caused by webs.
Two heads. It has advantage on Wisdom (Perception) checks and on saving throws against being blinded, charmed, deafened, frightened, stunned, or knocked unconscious.
Dire Den awareness. It senses intruders who enter its domain and cannot be surprised by them.

gm.title: Actions
lines:
Bite. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit, reach 5 ft., one creature. On a hit, deal 7 (1d8 + 3) piercing damage. The target makes a DC 11 Constitution save, taking 9 (2d8) poison damage on a failure or half on a success. If the poison damage reduces it to 0 HP, it is stable and poisoned for 1 hour even after regaining HP. It is paralyzed while poisoned this way.
Web (Recharge 5–6). Ranged weapon attack, +5 to hit, range 30/60 ft., one creature. A hit restrains the target in webbing. The target can use its action to make a DC 12 Strength check and break the web on a success. The web can also be attacked to destroy it. It has AC 10 and 5 HP, is vulnerable to fire, and is immune to bludgeoning, poison, and psychic damage.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: It waits with two ordinary giant spiders. It blocks the chamber entrance while they approach along the walls or ceiling. They fight to the death and do not follow fleeing prey.

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A gray-black wild-boar lookalike with short woolly hair, a bristled mane along its spine, rust-red eyes, and curved lower tusks up to 12 in. long. It stands about 3 ft. at the shoulder.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Morale average (8–10). Semi-intelligent (2–4). No treasure, special defenses or magic resistance. The entry gives no special creature saving throw.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix, pp. 103–104.

gm.title: Attacks
lines: One attack per round for 3d4 damage. It charges a bearer of red steel or cinnabryl, often with Spikes active, and ignores the trick of distracting it with a few dropped red steel spikes.

gm.title: Eating metal
lines: Detects cinnabryl, red steel and steel seed by scent from up to 90 ft. Make a successful attack roll to touch an item made of these metals. On contact it immediately crumbles into edible powder. A weapon of one of those metals that hits the succulus makes contact and is subject to the same disintegration procedure. A magical item with a listed weapon or armor bonus has a 10% chance per +1 to resist. Other magical items made from the listed metals count as +2 (20%). Feeding takes one round regardless of the meal size.

gm.title: Dig and Spikes Legacies
lines: Both are always present. Each is usable three times a day. Digging removes a 5-ft. cube of earth, sand or mud within 10 ft. in one round. A creature within 1 ft. of the pit must pass a Dexterity check or fall inside. A pit in loose earth or mud soon collapses. The appendix’s monster Spikes rules last one round per HD (five rounds). A creature touching the caster takes 2d4 damage. Add 1d6 to a natural physical attack other than a bite. A cinnabryl-rich diet usually protects the succulus from Affliction.

gm.title: Encounters and ecology
lines: Rare family group of 1d12, active by day. Most are encountered with wild swine. Each encounter has a 5% chance of one half-strength offspring, with no separate juvenile stat block in the book. Two succuli produce a succulus. Offspring of a succulus and wild swine have a 5% chance to be a succulus. Eats ore but prefers refined metal. The metal-laden flesh is inedible. Cured hide can make armor equivalent to studded leather (AC 7). A trained young succulus can locate cinnabryl deposits.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The creature entry calls the two Legacies Dig and Spikes, and uses singular Spike in the combat prose. Digging is the Campaign Book name. This profile uses the appendix’s monster form of Spikes.

gm.title: Hit point rule
lines: Roll 3d8 + 1 for hit points using the appendix’s d8 Hit Dice rule.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A large tapir-like animal with green leathery skin, short snout, beady eyes, short ears and clawed webbed feet. It is 6 to 8 ft. long.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: AC 5 in animal form or 0 in tree form. Morale average (8–10). Animal intelligence (1). No treasure or magic resistance. The entry gives no separate saving throw against its attacks.

gm.title: Printed source

gm.title: Attacks
lines: Three standard attacks, claw/claw/bite for 1d4, 1d4 and 1d8. The table separately lists Forefeet for 1d6 as a special attack. The Combat text says it lashes out with its forefeet in water and uses all four attacks.

gm.title: Plant Form Legacy
lines: After failing a morale check in combat with no apparent way to flee, it takes one round to become a tree. Usually a bald cypress, or a tree suited to its rain forest. The tree is indistinguishable from an ordinary tree, has AC 0, and does not bleed when harmed. Weapon attacks to tree form do at most 1 damage total per round. It stays in tree form up to six hours a day. Plant Form prevents movement, speech and spellcasting under the Campaign Book Legacy rules. It does not need cinnabryl.

gm.title: Cover and retreat
lines: A swampmare has a 30% chance to hide in shadows in thick vegetation. If threatened, it may squeal and flee into water.

gm.title: Encounters and ecology
lines: Uncommon, solitary organization, 3d4 appearing, daytime activity. Gurrash breed domestic strains as mounts and pack animals, each large enough for one gurrash rider. It eats leaves, fruit and other vegetation and needs at least two hours of sunlight daily. Three or more hours in tree form in strong sunlight feed it for a day. Older swampmares spend more time as trees and typically take permanent tree form when they die of old age.

gm.title: Source notes
lines: The printed attack table gives three routine attacks and a separate Forefeet special attack. The combat prose gives four attacks in water without spelling out the individual roll sequence. The 1d6 Forefeet line supplies the damage for the extra attack when applying the water exception.

gm.title: Traits
lines:
Innate Spellcasting (Psionics). Intelligence, save DC 13, with no components. The swarm casts only while above half HP. Command, Comprehend Languages, and Detect Thoughts are at will. Confusion and Dominate Monster are each once per day, with expended uses recovered after a long rest.
Swarm. The swarm and other creatures can occupy the same space. It fits through any opening a Tiny rat could use. It cannot regain HP or gain temporary HP.
Telepathic Shroud. The swarm is immune to effects that would sense its emotions or read its thoughts and to all divination spells.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bites. Melee weapon attack +5 to hit, reach 0 ft., one target in the swarm’s space. A hit deals 14 (4d6) piercing damage. At half HP or lower it deals 7 (2d6) piercing instead.

gm.title: Damage and condition defenses
lines: Resists bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. Immune to charmed, frightened, grappled, paralyzed, petrified, prone, restrained, and stunned.

gm.title: Bonus actions
lines: Illumination. Shed dim light within 5 ft. of the swarm, increase it to bright light in a 5- to 20-ft. radius with the same distance of dim light beyond that, or extinguish it.

gm.title: 2014 spell procedures
lines:
Command, at will. Action, 60 ft., one visible creature. On a failed DC 13 Wisdom save it follows a one-word order on its next turn. It must understand the language. Undead and directly harmful commands are ineligible. The spell ends if the target cannot comply. The DM resolves orders outside the listed examples. Approach ends the turn when it reaches within 5 ft. of the swarm by the shortest route. Drop ends the turn after dropping held items. Flee spends the turn moving away as quickly as it can. Grovel drops it prone and ends the turn. Halt prevents movement and actions, with minimum flight allowed if needed to stay aloft.
Comprehend Languages, at will. Action, self, 1 hour. Understand literal spoken language the swarm hears and writing it sees while touching the written surface. Read one page per minute. It cannot decode ciphers or signs outside a written language.
Detect Thoughts, at will. Action, self, concentration up to 1 minute. Read the surface thoughts of a visible creature within 30 ft. The creature must have Intelligence 4 or higher and speak a language. On a later action, switch targets or probe deeper. A probe alerts the target, which makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. Success ends the spell. Failure reveals reasoning, emotional state, and a major concern. A probed creature can use an action to end the spell by winning an Intelligence contest against the swarm while it remains the focus. On casting or as an action the swarm can also search for eligible unseen minds within 30 ft., then read them while in range. Two feet of rock, 2 inches of non-lead metal, or a thin sheet of lead blocks that search.
Confusion, 1/day. Action, 90 ft., concentration up to 1 minute. Each creature in a 10-ft.-radius sphere around a point in range makes a DC 13 Wisdom save. A failure prevents reactions and requires a d10 at the start of each turn. On 1, roll a d8 for direction and spend all movement going that way without acting. On 2–6, the creature stays still and does nothing. On 7–8, it spends its action on one melee attack against a random creature in reach. If there is none, it does nothing. On 9–10, it moves and acts as usual. A DC 13 Wisdom save at the end of its turn ends the effect on that creature.
Dominate Monster, 1/day. Action, 60 ft., a visible creature, concentration up to 1 hour. The target makes a DC 13 Wisdom save, with advantage if the swarm or its allies are fighting it. Failure charms it. While conscious and on the same plane, the swarm can issue simple commands by telepathy without an action. If orders run out it protects itself. The swarm can spend an action for precise control through the end of its next turn and can spend its own reaction to direct the target’s reaction. Each time the target takes damage, another DC 13 Wisdom save can end the spell.

gm.title: HP threshold
lines: With its printed maximum of 36 HP, the swarm can cast at 19 HP or more. At 18 HP or less, use the smaller Bites damage.

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: The rats combine their memories and minds when they swarm and communicate as one. A rat separated from the swarm begins with Intelligence 15, loses 1 Intelligence per day to a minimum of 4, and returns to 15 when it rejoins any such swarm. Illithid colonies can receive a swarm’s reports within the elder brain’s telepathic range.

gm.title: Source notes
lines:
The swarm’s Telepathic Shroud covers all divination spells. The same block lists Detect Thoughts and Comprehend Languages, both self-range divinations, with no explicit self-cast exception. Both printed rules are retained.
The 2014 Command language and harmful-order restrictions still apply. Volo grants component-free casting and separately lists telepathy 30 ft.

lines:

lines: Environment. Temperate plains. Organization. Solitary, pair, or herd (5–8). It is about 25 ft. long and can weigh about 20,000 lb. The combat prose favors charging larger intruders and trampling smaller opponents. Treasure none. Advancement. 17–32 HD (Huge), 33–48 HD (Gargantuan). Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines:
Powerful Charge (Ex). A Gore made as part of a charge deals 4d8 + 20 damage. Apply the usual charge modifiers.
Trample (Ex). As a full-round action, move up to twice speed, or 60 ft., and run over opponents at least one size smaller. A creature is trampled when the triceratops covers its whole space. Deal 2d12 + 15 bludgeoning damage once per target per round. A trampled opponent can make an attack of opportunity at −4, or attempt a DC 28 Reflex save for half. A partially covered larger space permits the −4 attack of opportunity without trampling. If it ends in an illegal space, return it to its most recent legal position or the nearest legal position if closer.

lines: A dark grey dust bunny that blends into ordinary floor dust. Colonies look like several loose clumps of lint.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: 4d6 appearing. Very rare. Colony. Any activity cycle. Animal intelligence (1). Unreliable morale (2–4). No treasure or magic resistance.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: TSR, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix (1996), pp. 112–113.

gm.title: Combat
lines: One attack, 0 direct damage. A trosip attacks only sleepers and stays still whenever someone is awake within the range of its senses. It senses motion and vibration out to 60 ft., including invisible creatures. It moves silently 95% of the time.

gm.title: Suffocation
lines: At least four trosips are needed to attack one man-sized sleeper effectively. The victim saves vs. paralyzation using only magical protection bonuses. A failed save means death from suffocation in 1d4 + 1 rounds. A success wakes the victim in time to wave them away. If more than twelve trosips attack one victim, both of two saving throws must succeed for the victim to survive.

gm.title: Detection and retreat
lines: A stationary trosip looks like ordinary dust. Magic or devices that detect invisible creatures can reveal it, and some animals such as cats can see it. The colony withdraws once the victim wakes or the body begins cooling. The book describes fast short spurts and poor sustained movement.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Colonies feed on refuse and draw heat from sleepers. One trosip can multiply into 24 or more within a few days. Infants, young children and the infirm are especially vulnerable.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Immune to all effects of the Red Curse.

gm.title: Reading Black Flag stat blocks
lines:
Rules source. Black Flag Reference Document, Monsters.
The printed modifiers and fixed HP are ready to use. For a Dexterity (Stealth) check to avoid the creature, use its Perception value as the DC. For a Wisdom (Perception) check to detect it, use its Stealth value as the DC.
Condition resistance gives advantage on checks and saves to avoid or end the named condition. Condition vulnerability gives disadvantage. Apply damage resistance and vulnerability to the amount of damage instead.

lines: A swallowed creature is grappled. The tyrannosaurus is free to act. A swallowed creature can use a light slashing or piercing weapon to deal 25 damage to the gizzard (AC 12) and cut free. lines: All voats have a Legacy. Most suffer its Affliction and many have Phase. The Phase Affliction gives them soft, distorted flesh and makes them tend to sink into solid matter if they stay in place. They seldom wear cinnabryl and may get trace amounts from scarlet pimpernel.

gm.title: Phase Legacy
lines: If the voat has Phase, it can pass through solid matter for 1 round, up to three times daily once the Legacy is fully active. It can walk without sinking during deliberate phasing. The full effect is immune to solid weapons while phased, but magic missile, the Missile Legacy and magical fire, cold and electricity can still affect it. The Affliction and active Legacy are separate effects.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Packs raid granaries and ship cargo, gnaw through planks, and foul what they leave. They also nest in caves containing scarlet pimpernels. Nests may hold bright objects and gear from victims. Voats live 2–4 years and typically have 3–5 litters a year of 8–12. Cardinal ticks often infest them, and packs sometimes associate with Saragón lyra birds.

Additional rule references: Appendix pp. 4, 6–8 and Savage Coast Campaign Book Part 2 pp. 85, 96 and 104 for Class C flight and Legacy procedures.

gm.title: Combat
lines: When it can rear up, the vulturehound makes three attacks: two front talons for 1d3 each and one beak for 1d4. If it cannot rear, use the beak alone. In flight, it attacks with its front talons. It loses flight after losing more than 75% of starting HP. At exactly 75% loss, it can still fly. Class C movement requires at least half speed, allows a 90-degree turn per round and permits an aerial attack pass every two rounds.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: Renardy packs acquire Legacies but never suffer Affliction. Yazak Steppes populations lie outside the Red Curse’s direct influence. The text lists Gas Breath, Acid Touch, Gaseous Form and Sleep as common choices. Assign the individual’s Legacy before play.

gm.title: Common Legacies
lines: A fully active Legacy has up to three uses per day. Use the adult’s 2 HD as caster level. Gas Breath lasts up to 2 rounds before expiring and delivers one 1d4 poison hit to a target within 5 ft. Magical poison protection can grant a save vs. poison for half. Acid Touch is instantaneous and deals 1d4 + 2 on a successful hit against plant matter or flesh. Gaseous Form lasts 2 rounds with flight 3 (B), can pass through gaps that are not airtight, and can be driven by normal or magical winds. Most attacks cannot affect it. Magical fire, electricity, magic missile and the Missile Legacy can. Sleep lasts 4 rounds, targets one living creature closest to a location within 10 yards, and allows a save vs. spell.

gm.title: Pack and pups
lines: Packs hunt out of a den and drag back food. Their lair has a 50% chance to hold 3d4 pups. A pup has 1d4 HP, cannot fly, and bites for 1d2 damage. Pups taken young can be trained for war or hunting. A trained adult tracks as a 5th-level ranger or adds +3 to a ranger companion’s tracking skill. Each vulturehound has a 50% chance of cardinal ticks.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Vulturehounds take carrion and hunt isolated or sick prey. They watch and scent for carrion and bay like dogs. They are immune to vermilia. One animal yields enough blood for 1d6 doses of antivermilia medicine, made by a mage of at least 9th level with an alchemical laboratory. A dose cures a man-sized or smaller creature. The book says doses often cost over 150 gp.

lines:

lines: During the first attack, a DC 20 Wisdom (Perception) check detects the two eels. The eels surprise the travelers and sailors if nobody notices them. An eel dives and flees at 10 HP or fewer. lines:

Agile Landing (any Medium wildcat). Ignore falls of 40 ft. or less unless Incapacitated.
Deadly Bite (lion, tiger, or jaguar). A Bite hit against a Prone target is a critical hit.
Desert Dweller (sand cat). Ignore difficult terrain from dirt or sand and tolerate temperatures up to 120°F. Fresh food meets the cat's need for water.
Mountain Dweller (lynx or snow leopard). Ignore difficult terrain from snow, ice, or steep slopes.
Superior Sprint (cheetah or sand cat, 2 uses per short or long rest). When the cat moves on its turn in combat, it can quadruple its speed until the turn ends. Replaces Sprint.
Pack Tactics (lion). The cat has advantage on attacks against a target within 5 ft. of at least one ally of the cat, as long as the ally is not Incapacitated.
Powerful Leap (caracal, cougar, lion, margay, serval, or snow leopard). Double all jump distances, with or without a running start. Use either Strength or Dexterity to determine the distance.
Swimmer (tiger, leopard, ocelot, or jaguar). Gain a swim speed of 30 ft.

gm.title: Encounter
lines: Six winter wolves attack from the mist. They retreat into cover between attacks and focus on prone characters. The icy ground is difficult terrain and imposes disadvantage on saves to avoid falling prone. The wolves circle a fortified camp, harry sentries and prevent sleep. Characters who cannot sleep gain one level of exhaustion. If any reach two levels of exhaustion, the wolves attack. The pack gives up if the party gets 8 miles from the campsite. To run for it, count the party as having traveled 8 hours. At the end of each additional hour, each character makes a Constitution save at DC 10 plus hours traveled past 8 or gains one exhaustion level. Eluding the wolves awards 250 XP per character.

gm.title: Party strength
lines: The encounter adjustments do not stack. Weak removes one Winter Wolf. Strong increases Cold Breath to a DC 13 save and 27 cold damage. Very Strong makes the same breath change and adds one Winter Wolf. The Very Weak line says to remove two Dire Wolves even though the main encounter lists six Winter Wolves.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A long-legged gray wolf with upright ears, a narrow muzzle, a mottled coat and a bushy tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Initiative +2. AC is 14 (+2 Dex, +2 natural), touch 12, flat-footed 12. Space/reach 5 ft./5 ft.. Base attack +1. Grapple +2. Fortitude +5, Reflex +5, Will +1.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Revised v3.5 SRD, MonstersAnimals.rtf, Wolf. https://www.d20srd.org/srd/monsters/wolf.htm

gm.title: Special qualities
lines:
Low-light vision. See twice as far as a human in dim illumination while retaining color and detail.
Scent. Detect opponents by smell within 30 ft., or 60 ft. upwind and 15 ft. downwind. Strong odors double those ranges and overpowering odors triple them. A move action identifies the direction of a scent. At 5 ft. or closer, pinpoint the source.
With Track, a fresh scent trail typically starts at Survival DC 10. The DC rises by 2 per hour of age, subject to odor strength and the number of creatures. Surface and visibility modifiers do not apply to scent tracking.

gm.title: Skills and feats
lines:
Skills. Hide +2, Listen +3, Move Silently +3, Spot +3, Survival +1. Add a +4 racial bonus to Survival when tracking by scent.
Feats. Track (bonus feat), Weapon Focus (bite).

gm.title: Encounter ecology
lines: Environment. Temperate forests. Organization. Solitary, pair, or pack (7–16). A pack may engage from the front while others circle to the flanks or rear. Treasure none. Advancement. 3 HD (Medium), 4–6 HD (Large). Level adjustment none listed.

gm.title: Special attacks
lines: Trip (Ex). When Bite hits, the wolf can try to trip a Large or smaller opponent as a free action. Use its +1 Strength check modifier, opposed by the target’s better Strength or Dexterity modifier, with the normal size and stability adjustments. This needs no touch attack and provokes no attack of opportunity. If it wins, the target falls prone. If it loses, the opponent gets no countertrip.

lines: 1 appearing. Very rare, common in Robrenn. Solitary carnivore. Any activity cycle. Animal intelligence (1). Treasure J, K, L, M, N. Steady morale (11–12). No magic resistance or special defenses.

lines:
TSR, Savage Coast Monstrous Compendium Appendix (1996), pp. 122–123. 
Additional rule references: Appendix pp. 6–7 and Savage Coast Campaign Book Part 2 pp. 85 and 88 for uses, effective level and general Bite duration.

gm.title: Combat
lines: One ordinary bite for 1d3 damage. The wynzet usually allows petting and feeding. It wins a forest despoiler’s trust before launching its special throat bite.

gm.title: Bite Legacy
lines: Once it has befriended a despoiler, it can leap up to 15 ft. for the throat attack at +4 to hit. On the first successful attack, the target saves vs. paralyzation with Dexterity bonuses. Failure kills the target. Success still deals 2d8 damage. Later attacks deal 1d8 with the active Legacy or 1d3 with the ordinary bite.

gm.title: Red Curse
lines: All wynzets have the Bite Legacy and require no cinnabryl. The general Bite Legacy lasts 1 round per level. At 1 HD the duration is 1 round, up to three activations daily when fully active. The entry specifies the special first hit and does not give a separate reset trigger.

gm.title: Ecology
lines: Robrenn’s druids empower these woodland guardians. They breed as the creature they resemble, and about 5% of their offspring are wynzets. A despoiler’s remains replenish the forest. In Renardy the beast is sometimes called le lapin mortel.

Yum. A Small or larger creature can spend an action to eat a living yumgrub within 5 ft. The yumgrub dies. For 1 minute the eater doubles its speed and gains +4 to Strength and +2 to AC. When the minute ends, the eater gains two levels of Exhaustion.

gm.title: Actions
lines: Bite (group attack). Melee weapon attack, −1 to hit, reach 5 ft., one target. Hit 1 piercing damage per participant.

gm.title: MCDM minion rules
lines:
Minions of the same stat block normally share a turn and can all move before taking their actions. They use fixed damage, cannot score critical hits, and have no Hit Dice to spend.
A minion drops to 0 HP if an attack damages it or it takes damage from failing a save. Other damage kills it if the damage meets or exceeds its maximum HP. Otherwise the minion ignores that damage.
Overkill. When a weapon hit deals more damage than a minion’s maximum HP, apply the excess to an additional minion of the same stat block, as weapon attack damage. Repeat while damage remains after subtracting each target’s maximum HP. Melee targets must be within reach of the attack. Ranged targets must lie along the line of the attack and within the weapon’s normal range. Opportunity attacks cannot overkill.
Group attack. Two to five minions of the same stat block sharing a turn can each spend their action to make one attack if the target is within reach or range of each participant. Roll once, adding +1 for each participant, and multiply the fixed damage by that same count on a hit. Use advantage or disadvantage only if it applies to everyone in the group. Split groups when the target has different cover or concealment from different attackers.
A minion can make a group attack alone using its listed attack bonus and damage. If multiple eligible minions could make the same melee opportunity attack, they can each use their reaction to join one group attack. If the group attack triggers an effect against a single attacker, its target chooses which participating minion it affects.

gm.title: Appearance
lines: A compact equine with black and pale stripes, a short upright mane, rounded ears and a thin tufted tail.

gm.title: Other statistics
lines: Passive Perception 10. No listed languages or special senses.

gm.title: Printed source
lines: Wizards of the Coast, Tomb of Annihilation, First printing, September 2017, printed p. 106, p. 107. https://www.dndbeyond.com/sources/toa/dwellers-of-the-forbidden-city Uses Riding Horse, Monster Manual (2014), printed p. 336. https://www.dndbeyond.com/monsters/16997-riding-horse

gm.title: Actions
lines: Hooves. Melee weapon attack, +5 to hit against one target within 5 ft. A hit deals 8 (2d4 + 3) bludgeoning damage.

gm.title: Encounter notes
lines: Wongo’s Shrine gives the Zebra the Riding Horse statistics. When the shrine masks deliver their curse, anyone who looked through one in the last hour makes a DC 15 Constitution save. A failed save transforms the viewer into the animal on the last mask they used, as polymorph. The curse ends after 24 hours.

gm.title: Base-stat erratum
lines: First-print Monster Manual p. 336 gives Hooves +2 to hit for the Riding Horse. The official errata had corrected it to +5 by 2016. The 2017 Zebra reference uses the corrected Riding Horse block.

name: A bag with a forwarding address

gm.title: At the table
lines: Objects put in a bag appear in a former owner's washbasin. The washbasin keeper has begun labeling and selling the arrivals.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Grain runs short before winter. A retired ovensweeper who buys kiln ash to repair old mortar remembers bricking up the municipal grain store behind a bake oven. They will show the party where if the city promises to pay for the repairs.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An honest ally switches sides when an enemy buys their debt. Make their change of allegiance negotiable and let the party learn the terms.

name: A bargain with nobody left to collect

gm.title: At the table
lines: A villain keeps a borrowed talent until the other party receives the agreed payment. Find the lawful successor and ask whether they want the bargain fulfilled or renegotiated.

name: A basket full of unripe berries

gm.title: At the table
lines: Foragers are stripping a patch before its fruit is ready. Their village expects a hard frost and needs news from the weather tower.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The same light is an invitation on the way out and a distress call on the way back. A lighthouse keeper will share the signal book if the party helps repair the boat that takes them off shift.

name: A bell auction chooses who rings the thaw

gm.title: At the table
lines: The winning bidder rings in spring. Any fishing boat within earshot can launch that day without paying. The old bell has cracked and the new one can be heard from the disputed island, where the regular fee is still contested. Players can help decide whether to move it, repair the old bell, or require two signals.

name: A bellows draws in the marsh

gm.title: At the table
lines: One room smells of peat when a forge operates even though every chimney exits uphill. Pull the bellows when the forge is cold. Wet reeds catch on its intake grate. Behind the grate a broad duct descends to a flooded passage.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A wild boar uproots a strip of plants while ignoring all the others. A forager demonstrates how it is following a buried edible root.

name: A bone key leaves a debt

gm.title: At the table
lines: A key opens a single lock and breaks in it. Owners of locks opened this way can use the fragment to ask who turned it, which makes the key useful evidence as well as a shortcut.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Names disappear from a log while titles and salaries remain. A set of signed expense sheets can reconstruct who held each job.

name: A book moth connects two borrowers’ copies

gm.title: At the table
lines: Overnight the moth stitches together the first sheets of two books once owned by the same reader. A missing leaf was torn out of one of them. Follow the twitching thread before dawn to find where the moth tucked it.

name: A borrowed sled makes you responsible for its next passenger

gm.title: At the table
lines: The sled carries a visible customs token. Anyone traveling on it inherits responsibility for taking the next registered traveler through a checkpoint. Check who put a particular passenger on the list before getting underway.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bad smell rises only while the waterwheel turns. The miller will stop it if the party handles today's line of impatient customers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A proud brewer lets rivals name one missing ingredient before serving. One rival names a crop the council forbade planting last season.

name: A bulette waits for the loaded sledge

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fresh upheavals follow the tandem ruts, ending where a sledge was unloaded. The creature surfaces before the next loaded crossing. Move the supplies in smaller loads, use the bedrock shoulder, or send an empty sledge while someone watches where the ground moves.

name: A burning beard marks last call

gm.title: At the table
lines: A landlord sets a magical flame alight for the final round. Tonight it burns low and blue after the firewood merchant arrives.

name: A buyer wants the old dents left in

gm.title: At the table
lines: A collector seeks family ornaments pawned during a bad winter and pays extra to keep two characteristic dents visible. A stoneworker can match the marks to a setting tool still used in one atelier. The repair book can lead to the buyers.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Local travelers leave carved signs to say whether the camp is safe. Someone added a fresh sign upside down.

name: A canceled debt still guarantees someone else’s loan

gm.title: At the table
lines: The party can erase a local worker’s debt by tearing up its contract. A note in the margin shows that the debt also backs a ferry repair loan. Bring both parties to the lender to substitute a different guarantee, or let the cancellation stand and help the ferry find another source of credit.

name: A cart with one coffin too many

gm.title: At the table
lines: The burial clerk counts fewer names than crates. The driver wants someone's help tracing the delivery while keeping the horses moving.

name: A cat inhabits the fish scale

gm.title: At the table
lines: A cat ghost inhabits the counter scale at a fishmonger's stall. Let the party decide whether to spend a morning giving it the ordinary care nobody gave it in life.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A temporary illusion puts a mask on the drinker. It silently takes on the expression of whoever last handled the vial. The wearer can use a mirror to see what that person felt.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hungry child offers buttons to be escorted to a cookshop after dusk. The shopkeeper recognizes the buttons as tokens for staff meals.

name: A cistern frog keeps its understudy

gm.title: At the table
lines: One frog dives when the kitchen bell rings, and another calls while the first is underwater. The kitchen crew can tell which is calling. A stranger who tries to slip across the yard between calls hears a third frog answering under the floor.

name: A city's night shift mislays its sunrise

gm.title: At the table
lines: Lamplighters argue over who should extinguish their last street when an artificial dawn starts halfway through the shift. Ask where it ends and follow the contiguous lit street to the device being tested, or help the workers make a temporary handover.

gm.title: At the table
lines: The elders can sweep an old influence past a ring of doors. Draw where the boundary will land and ask what it leaves outside.

name: A cold hand on warm wax

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hand feels cold enough to firm warm wax on contact. The cooling ends after it has set one small seal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A garrison's oath has lost its divine witness. Officers claim it still holds, while rank-and-file soldiers want a new agreement they can read before signing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An argument spills from a table to a packed street. One duelist wants witnesses and the other wants everyone gone.

name: A compass tuned to what was stolen

gm.title: At the table
lines: A compass points to a movable piece of iron. Documentary evidence says it was once calibrated against a fixed object that vanished.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A magician's cottage turns its doors away from the road whenever someone approaches quickly. A delivery person can model the greeting it recognizes.

name: A crab takes a small problem off the deck

gm.title: At the table
lines: The crab collects loose pegs and puts them in a box below the strongest nearby smell. A barrel owner swears the bilge plug was put back. Follow the crab to learn if the plug was removed or if the keeper is looking in the wrong compartment.

name: A credible compromise the villain refuses

gm.title: At the table
lines: Write down one exchange that would help both sides. Identify what keeps the opposition from taking it and give the party a way to change that condition.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A new field plant can ease pain, but it fruits only where a rare moth survives. The grain cooperative wants to plow the neighboring ditch.

name: A crown over a junk dealer's mark

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jeweled crown was plated over reused metal. A repair exposes part of a manufacturer's mark on the inside.

name: A crystal eye rides an empty boat

gm.title: At the table
lines: An artificial eye lies in the center of a skiff that stayed dry in an oily slick. Return it to its owner before the harbor sorts the boat as salvage, or trade the eye for an account of the slick.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guests throw a battered cup through hoops. The cup always renews itself by dawn, but one new piece bears an unfamiliar maker's mark.

name: A cupboard hinge repeats whichever side opened it

gm.title: At the table
lines: A creature nesting in a hinge makes a rising sound when the door opened from inside and a falling sound otherwise. It repeats only when the kitchen is empty. The party can wait beyond the closed kitchen door to hear the last opening while the staff look for a missing tray.

name: A curious monster brings a replacement

gm.title: At the table
lines: A large sea creature takes anything dropped overboard and brings back something of similar shape. The next object it offers marks a channel the boat cannot enter at its current draft.

name: A curse leaves empty nails in familiar houses

gm.title: At the table
lines: Any drawing hung in a house on the affected block is found standing upright at the ruins of the old courthouse by dawn. Copies of the same drawing congregate there. An intact framed map can show which parcels still count as part of the block.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A hex has shifted from shopkeeper to buyer. Both receipts give the buyer the right to a return, but every attempt to hand over the object shifts it again.

name: A dance beneath a quiet house

gm.title: At the table
lines: The upstairs owners enforce silence. Underground, dancers use steps to signal arrivals to someone posted in the alley.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A courtier refuses gifts because every past gift became a debt. Add one ally willing to help anonymously and one who needs public credit.

name: A deck pet marks who actually handled the crate

gm.title: At the table
lines: The ship's bird retrieves a polished peg when a familiar crate is unloaded and carries it to the person who removed the crate lid. Today it goes to the outgoing cook. Compare the cook’s account with the deck tally before assigning custody.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A dead investigator walks the same route seeking a witness who grew up and moved away. Find the witness under their adult name or show the ghost a later copy of the case.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A jewel reappears in the nearest tied purse whenever dropped. Search who packed the nearest tied container before the theft.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Residents begin changing shape whenever they trade coats at a particular stall. Pin down who wore each garment before the rain washes the labels away.

name: A dog guards an empty camp

gm.title: At the table
lines: A frightened dog defends a camp nobody has used for days. Returning the stray's missing collar settles it long enough to search.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Every guest enters in costume. Someone wearing the same mask as a party member arrived hours ago and paid for two seats.

name: A dragon changes altitude to make shelter for another flyer

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a juvenile tries a crossing, an older dragon circles low to force a steady upward draft in the gorge. Travelers who know the routine can cross in its wake or get out of the narrow road before the second pass.

name: A dragon courts through visible acts of upkeep

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each spring two dragons compete to finish the largest useful local repair. One moved a rock to change a stream and left a mill without power. The rival is interested in finishing the neglected work if locals agree they can judge the result.

name: A dragon keeps its molted scales for repairs

gm.title: At the table
lines: Weathered breast scales naturally fall onto a stone shelf. The dragon arranges them by season and uses the tough layers to bridge leaks in its lair ceiling. It trades a loose scale only after someone shows where the leak can be patched without it.

name: A dragon’s roof has two built-in routes for rainfall

gm.title: At the table
lines: Outside one stream feeds a safe pool. A concealed gutter diverts the other stream around a bed of fragile crystals. Look for a dry seam to find the hidden gutter. Tilt the slab toward the seam to divert water away from the crystals, or put it on the exposed channel to flood the route behind your group.

name: A drifting fence reveals the salt road

gm.title: At the table
lines: Fence posts slide in shallow salt crust as the wind turns, but four buried feet keep their original line. Check which posts rock and follow the fixed ones to a hard surface before moving the wagon.

name: A dryad offers seed instead of coin

gm.title: At the table
lines: A grove keeper offers a seed that will grow wherever the party deposits it. Taking the reward means deciding who gets to tend what grows.

name: A faction's dues fund one person the members never meet

gm.title: At the table
lines: A line in the membership register pays an absent specialist from each applicant's first month's dues. Follow the payments to the person who maintains the public wards. They offer to keep doing the work if the party can arrange a public stipend. Decide whether to disclose their former source of support before the council votes.

name: A familiar body carries a new tool

gm.title: At the table
lines: The party recognizes a dead traveler whose tools belong to a different trade. A guild mark leads to where they learned that trade.

name: A familiar greeting ends when someone mentions the change

gm.title: At the table
lines: A contact greets the party as usual while hiding a problem. Decide which thing they hope nobody will mention and how their greeting breaks off when someone does. The players can ask privately or bring the issue into the room.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A trusted merchant misses market for the first time in years. A neighboring seller has been asked to cash an unusual set of receipts on their behalf.

name: A farm keeps one room aired

gm.title: At the table
lines: An abandoned farm has every entrance blocked except the pantry vent. A yearly festival still stores something there as part of an old agreement.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bright feather releases heat the first time each person takes it. It has already cooled for someone who claims never to have seen it.

name: A fey village elects its last visitor

gm.title: At the table
lines: When a newcomer arrives, the preceding visitor becomes mayor until they can hand over the sash. The older mayor has let the roads go unmarked to postpone that moment. Find out what unfinished promise they lose the power to fulfill upon leaving office.

name: A fissure separates the mule team

gm.title: At the table
lines: A tremor leaves pack animals on a ledge with just enough room to stand still. The cargo has to come off first.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A flask stays full even when poured. The same amount disappears from a marked cistern that many people rely on.

name: A flower sends back a memory

gm.title: At the table
lines: Sleep beside the bloom to recall one detail from a forgotten place. Ask which detail the character looks for and give one image they can verify awake.

name: A forecast needs a witness in both places

gm.title: At the table
lines: A diviner and a willing contact physically present at the destination each see the same ten seconds of one possible future there. Each glimpse shows the other witness’s face. Give the diviner a choice of contacts with different terms for participating.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A traveler sets out birthday cakes for guests who won't arrive. The empty seats are marked with places the party can check.

name: A foundation shelters the town it displaced

gm.title: At the table
lines: The bridge footings were built above an old cluster of rooms. Light a candle in one upper opening and people below knock in answer. Clearing the public path would expose both a settlement and the safe way across at flood stage.

name: A front door can borrow the builder's shadow

gm.title: At the table
lines: The carpenter who hung the door can step through once a day without opening it. Tomorrow they retire, and the house can transfer the privilege only while both carpenters are present. The old carpenter wants one hour inside to recover their own work before the handover.

name: A fugitive asks for neutral ground

gm.title: At the table
lines: A former servant wants shelter and insists their old employer is coming. The host needs a neutral witness to offer protection lawfully.

name: A gate ring carries paint from a distant shutter

gm.title: At the table
lines: A scrap of yellow paint is trapped between the old ring and its housing. It matches a chipped shutter at a second site where the gate stood last month. Find the carpenter who moved the whole gate and ask why its ownership marks were left behind.

name: A ghost ship wants its passengers discharged

gm.title: At the table
lines: A spectral captain cannot dock until someone ashore signs the passenger manifest. The harbor office finds two names that already belong to living citizens.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A house ghost lets one living visitor see where its friend used to sit. It will leave if somebody who knows that friend publicly acknowledges the friendship.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An iridescent scale drifts against the current when wet. Floating it at a fork can narrow the search for the animal that shed it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A masterless construct follows house numbers in order and stops at every missing number. The oldest town map shows why one address was removed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A lonely grave has an epitaph addressed to whoever comes after a particular date. A second inscription is visible when the light falls low.

name: A guarantee follows a doorway instead of a trade

gm.title: At the table
lines: A shop legend says all work done at the address must be repaired there. Recent renovations moved the door without moving the shop. Two owners claim the guarantee shifted. Let the party ask who can demonstrate an old repair before settling which claimant gets the next fee.

name: A halo moves like a lantern

gm.title: At the table
lines: A halo visibly lights the wall above a barricade while its wearer stays behind it. Make the light obvious before anyone attempts to hide.

name: A harmless guest in the hand

gm.title: At the table
lines: A small animal appears briefly wherever the drinker holds out cupped hands. A boy recognizes it as the same species that ruined his flower bed.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Notes follow the drinker's voice and give away which words they emphasize. A bard can take down the pattern as a separate melody.

name: A healer asks where a mark was drawn

gm.title: At the table
lines: Two artists draw the same public decoration but place the small maker's dot on different edges. Their clients last week queued in different buildings. Find the booking list for the correct artist to learn who had contact with a missing person.

name: A hearth crab clicks for the table that feeds it

gm.title: At the table
lines: The crab patrols a tavern's hearthstone and retreats when strangers reach toward it. It accepts a saucer of brine and answers the knock pattern of the server that usually feeds it. Tonight someone in a private room knows that rhythm.

name: A heel print full of brick

gm.title: At the table
lines: A giant track contains shards from a kiln. The local masons can tell whether the giant came to rob them or happened to step in a collapsed wall.

name: A hill has a stair for every tax bracket

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each of three sets of stairs reaches the same tollhouse but was built under a different charter. The unused public stair can reopen if someone finds where a later landowner bricked up its lower arch.

name: A horned draft animal blocks the road

gm.title: At the table
lines: An armored wagon gives priority to its giant draft animal's rest. The traders will take detour advice if it reaches a place where the animal can turn around.

name: A hunter wants the correct culprit

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bounty hunter has a description that fits two people. They will split the reward for proof the one they caught is wrong.

name: A journeyman has tools from three closed shops

gm.title: At the table
lines: Each shop closed after the owner's legal address changed. The tools remain on three loan lists. They can be returned one by one or assembled to run the former shared workshop, with the borrowers choosing who keeps a key.

name: A knight wants a local cause

gm.title: At the table
lines: An eager knight asks about threats they can end before supper. The person doing the real work asks them to lend gear instead.

name: A large fish trails a line

gm.title: At the table
lines: A predator trails the vessel with a line caught on its fin. It only approaches when the ship slows. Cutting the line gives it a reason to leave and the party a marked hook to trace.

name: A lawn sinks where the new pitch says it should rise

gm.title: At the table
lines: The youngest groundskeeper can still reveal the former terrace line by rolling a ball downhill. A match roster is due tonight. Follow the line to the damaged drain or move a celebrated contest indoors and face the two clubs.

name: A letter of credit for a dead bank

gm.title: At the table
lines: An old letter can be redeemed at a bank nobody recalls. Paying out the value would restore the bank's charter and expose an existing debtor.

name: A letter sealed against its own opener

gm.title: At the table
lines: A purpose-made letter opener will slice anything except the envelope sold alongside it. Hold its edge to the stamp to reveal whose permission the seal requires.

name: A local legend has a different ending at each doorway

gm.title: At the table
lines: Shopkeepers tell visitors how the great fire stopped. Each knows the last thing they saw happen from their own doorway. Give the party two positions where the stories can both be right and a third where they can see what lay between.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A closed group keeps a new guest in a house with reinforced shutters. Neighbors hear the same toast every hour and know where the wine comes in.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A whirlpool opens a route to an underwater market at slack tide. The down-current entrance is safe only while a basalt marker is visible. The other route remains open but carries a toll.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A junk seller prices an enchanted object as everyday stock. An apprentice races to buy it back before their employer finds out.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A bird takes bright badges and keys but ignores coin. Its nest holds tokens from every halted road crew. The watch will change the locks by dawn if its key is still missing.

name: A maker quotes two prices for the same mug

gm.title: At the table
lines: One price includes lifetime repairs by the maker. The lower price comes with the recipe for the glaze so another worker can repair it. If asked, the maker will name which other shop has the correct kiln.

name: A map drawn for the tide

gm.title: At the table
lines: A route ends at a point apparently empty on land. It makes sense only against a chart that shows low-water obstructions.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A chest opens for one passerby per hour. Its offerings provide exactly what a person needs to commit an act the market would condemn.

name: A midpoint that gives away leverage

gm.title: At the table
lines: Introduce a discovery that changes what people can ask for without dictating what the party should do. Let it reopen at least one route that looked closed in the first act.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Thousands of beetles travel in a straight line at dusk. Campers can pack up or learn which ordinary scent sends them around the tents.

name: A minute to see unseen guests

gm.title: At the table
lines: A drink reveals creatures using invisibility for a minute. An opaque barrier still hides whatever stands behind it.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A desert inn only appears when a traveler gives up looking for it. A regular has left supplies outside the door for people who cannot bring themselves to stop.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Children disappear along one school route. A retired crossing guard remembers when the missing group started leaving a seat empty on purpose.

name: A missing tool turns up ahead

gm.title: At the table
lines: An object misplaced on the trail appears farther ahead already worn with use. A second object can be left behind to repeat the test.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Nobody remembers who kept the last watch. The mud records which boots went outside and which fire was burning.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A loose fence panel acts like an impassable border for a particular family. A land charter gives the terms under which it can be relocated.

name: A mute instrument knows the rhythm

gm.title: At the table
lines: An instrument plays silently but moves dust along the sounding board. One nearby musician can read the arrangement by watching the dust.

name: A naked runner and a uniform

gm.title: At the table
lines: Guards chase a streaker who refuses a cloak because it carries a stolen badge. The crowd thinks the badge belongs to the guard doing the chasing.

gm.title: At the table
lines: An illegal fishing boat snared a merfolk messenger. Opening the holding tank will free the messenger and lose evidence of the catch. Find a way to preserve a witness, the ship's log, or the net before opening it.

name: A noble announces the wrong news

gm.title: At the table
lines: A public address reads an announcement meant for tomorrow. Copies posted at the city gates bear a different seal.

gm.title: At the table
lines: Treat a famine, disputed law, or migration as a force that changes people's choices. Put two people in charge of different responses and let players influence which response can spread.

name: A nose for an older visitor

gm.title: At the table
lines: The drinker distinguishes recent smells from older ones. Given an object that carries a reference scent, they can recognize it in a crowded room.

gm.title: At the table
lines: A preacher recruits in the market and includes a detail from a private conversation. A gap in the crowd provides a line of sight to the person feeding it to them.

name: A peddler who keeps asking directions

gm.title: At the table
lines: A persistent peddler names a different local landmark every time they approach. These are addresses being tested in front of someone who follows them.

name: A performer remembers the audience by seating
